title: Sobolev Regularized Score Difference Estimation in Diffusion Models
claim: Directly modeling the difference between two score functions yields a far smoother, lower-variance field than modeling an absolute score.
layout: 2 side-by-side vector-field panels, each with its own norm colorbar
description: Two side-by-side 2-D quiver plots over x1 and x2 in [-2, 2], each with a viridis colorbar labelled 'norm'. The left panel, titled 'Velocity Field: ∇log q', shows a dense, chaotic radial burst of arrows. They converge on two sinks near (-0.2, 0) and (1, 0), and the norm runs up to about 25. The right panel, titled 'Velocity Field: ∇log(q/p)', shows nearly uniform horizontal arrows in evenly spaced rows. Their norm is lower, at most about 12, and they vary little. The eye goes first to the tangled left panel, then to the orderly right one. The contrast in smoothness and magnitude is the whole point, and no text annotations beyond the titles are needed.
caption: Visualization of the score functions. The score difference field (right) is markedly smoother and less variable than the absolute target score (left), demonstrating the structural benefit of directly estimating the score difference.
abstract: Estimating the difference of two Stein's score functions is a fundamental problem in generative modeling. In particular, score differences arise naturally in transfer learning, where the score difference provides the mechanism for adapting a pre-trained model to a new target distribution, and in diffusion model-based post-training methods such as discriminator guidance. Existing estimators for score differences in these settings either lack of statistical consistency or are difficult to scale up in high-dimensions. We propose a statistically consistent and scalable estimator for score differences based on Sobolev regularization, which plays a crucial role in ensuring consistency and stablizing the training in the small-sample regime. Mathematically, we establish a convergence rate of $O(n^{-\frac{s-1}{d+2s-2}})$ where $d$ is the dimension and $s$ denotes the smoothness of the underlying densities, and provide a minimax lower bound of $\tildeÎ©(n^{-\frac{2(s-1)}{d+2s}})$ (in mean-squared error). Empirically, our estimator exhibits significantly improved stability in small-sample regimes compared to existing methods. We demonstrate its effectiveness on real-world tasks, including transfer learning for ECG signal generation, where it substantially outperforms non-regularized score difference estimators in downstream classification performance.
